title: Anomaly-based per-tenant ingest-latency detection + lightweight tracing snapshots
creator: Priya Nair
description: Background: The analytics ingest pipeline occasionally exhibits short-lived latency regressions that impact downstream console dashboards and cost aggregation jobs. Existing alerts are global and threshold-based which leads to long detection windows or noise when a small number of tenants experience issues. Goal: Implement anomaly-based detection of ingest latency at tenant granularity and capture lightweight tracing snapshots when anomalies are detected so on-call and owners can quickly triage root cause.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant SLI for ingest latency (p95 over 5m) is emitted with tenant_id tag for >95% of traffic
Anomaly detector identifies sustained regressions (relative deviation and change-point) and creates alerts with tenant context
When an anomaly is triggered, system attaches a sampled set of lightweight tracing snapshots (<=10 spans) to the alert and links to the tenant timeline
Dashboards show per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency heatmap and a filtered view for alerted tenants
False positive rate measured in first 2 weeks is <10% and runbook describes escalation and suppression steps
tasks: Instrument ingest service to emit latency histogram with tenant_id tag and consistent bucket boundaries
Add low-cardinality tenant metadata and a high-cardinality tag route for owners only (to control costs)
Implement streaming anomaly detector job (kafka consumer) that computes rolling baselines and fires alerts
Add tracing snapshot hook: when detector flags tenant, trigger lightweight trace sampler to capture single request trace samples and store pointer in alert payload
Create Grafana dashboards and a templated tenant view + heatmap panel
Write PagerDuty/Slack integration mapping and automated suppression window policy
Complete e2e test with synthetic tenants and load generator, validate detector sensitivity and snapshot attachment
Publish runbook and add to on-call rotation checklist
comments: 2025-02-18 - Priya Nair: Triage note: several customer incidents last quarter were caused by short per-tenant backpressure spikes. Global SLOs masked localized problems. Proposing anomaly-based approach + trace snapshots to reduce MTTR.

2025-02-20 - Mateo Alvarez: Design review completed with Observability team. Decided on rolling baseline window of 3h and alert cooldown of 30m. Need to be careful about cardinality — will emit tenant_id only on summary histograms, not raw spans.

2025-02-25 - Lina Park (Observability): Reviewed detector proto. Suggested adding both relative change and CUSUM change-point detection to reduce sensitivity to diurnal patterns. Also requested an index in metrics store for tenant_id to keep query performance acceptable.

2025-02-28 - Mateo Alvarez: Initial instrumentation PR submitted: github.com/redwood/ingest-service/pull/1842. Adds tenant_histogram metric and a lightweight trace-snapshot API. PR link: https://github.com/redwood/ingest-service/pull/1842

2025-03-01 - QA (Diego Ramos): Running synthetic traffic job against staging. Observed detector firing on test tenant when latency increased by 35% sustained over 10m. Trace snapshots linked correctly in alert payload. Two tweak items: increase histogram bucket at 200ms and add tenant alias resolution in alert message.

2025-03-04 - Mateo Alvarez: Deployed detector worker to canary cluster (10% of traffic). Added Grafana dashboard panels: per-tenant heatmap, alert timeline, and sampled trace viewer. Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/analytics/ingest-latency-heatmap

2025-03-05 - Priya Nair: Next: run 2-week observation window to measure false positives, refine thresholds, and prepare runbook for rotation. Also coordinate with Dedicated team to ensure private deployments have the same metric schema mapping.
